(gusperimus) Profile Gusperimus is a guanidine derivative that inhibits both cell-me- diated and antibody-mediated immunity. It is used in the treat- ment of renal graft rejection, and has been investigated in the management of graft-versus-host disease and Wegener’s granu- lomatosis. For mention of its role in reversing acute graft rejec- tion in kidney transplantation, see p.1813. Gusperimus is used as the hydrochloride. A dose of 3 to 5 mg/kg of gusperimus hydrochloride given daily for 7 days, by intrave- nous infusion over 3 hours, has been suggested in the treatment of acute renal graft rejection. Treatment may be continued for a further 3 days if required. Rapid injection should be avoided as an acute in- crease in plasma concentration may produce respiratory depres- sion. ◊ References. 1. Ramos EL, et al.
